survey: Stage spotlight hanging from a lighting truss. The truss is a two-tube ladder truss with zigzag diagonal braces welded between the upper and lower tubes; it crosses the top of the frame, with tube ends visible on the left and the truss running off-frame on the right. A dark hanging clamp hooks over the upper tube and drops in front of the lower tube, held by a bolt. From the clamp hangs a U-shaped yoke; each arm ends at a round pivot knob on the side of the lamp, roughly level with the body's center of mass, so the lamp can tilt. The lamp is a cylinder with vent slots on top and an orange trim band. Its front lens holds three LEDs (yellow, cyan, red), facing down-left toward the camera, with colored beams leaving in that direction. Everything hangs from one supported point, the yoke is symmetric, the counts make sense (two pivots, one clamp, three emitters), and the beams go the way the lamp faces. The missing power cable is an acceptable simplification.
